relevance_reason: This review by the group that first described MAGIS syndrome summarises the clinical frequencies in their original 20-patient cohort, two families with autosomal dominant transmission, the GNAI2 gain-of-function mechanisms and the outcome of HSCT in one patient.

findings.statement: Lamborn et al. (2025) reviewed MAGIS syndrome, an inborn error of immunity caused by heterozygous germline activating mutations in GNAI2. They described it as an acronym for midline malformations of the brain, anterior pituitary gland dysfunction, growth retardation, immunodysregulation/immunodeficiency, and skeletal defects. They noted considerable phenotypic heterogeneity, with nearly all patients showing both immune and nonimmune features.
quotes: MAGIS ("Midline malformations of the brain, Anterior pituitary gland dysfunction, Growth retardation, Immunodysregulation/immunodeficiency, and Skeletal defects") caused by heterozygous germline activating mutations in GNAI2 (encoding the heterotrimeric G-protein, Gαi2)
Broadly, nearly all patients display both immune and nonimmune disease features, but with variable severity.

findings.statement: Lamborn et al. (2025) summarized nonimmune features in their original cohort of 20 patients from 18 families with GNAI2 mutations. Features were: growth retardation in 90% (IUGR 53%, postnatal short stature 90%); low IGF1 in 8 of 11 tested; growth hormone deficiency in 7 of 7 formally tested; structural or functional anterior pituitary defects in 59%; midline brain malformations in 30% (including corpus callosum agenesis or hypoplasia, cerebellar and pons hypoplasia, and Chiari I malformation); skeletal dysostoses in 85%; and dysmorphism in 100%. They noted that rare features such as coloboma or subcortical band heterotopia should raise suspicion for MAGIS.
quotes: Among these, growth retardation is most penetrant (90%), manifesting as both prenatal intrauterine growth restriction (IUGR; 53%) and postnatal short stature (90%), as well as low serum insulin-like growth factor-1 (8 of 11 tested, 73%) and growth hormone deficiency (7 of 7 formally tested).
Further endocrinological evaluation has revealed that structural (41%) or functional (53%) defects of the anterior pituitary gland are present in 59% of patients.
Skeletal defects comprise diverse craniofacial, appendicular, and axial skeletal dysostoses affecting 85% of patients and underlie the high prevalence of dysmorphia (100%).

findings.statement: Lamborn et al. (2025) reported immune-mediated disease in 95% of the cohort: immunodeficiency in 90% and immune dysregulation in 50% (systemic autoinflammation 15%, autoimmunity 35%, splenomegaly 35%). Infections were mainly sinopulmonary (respiratory tract 75%, middle ear 65%, sinuses 35%), cutaneous (25%) and invasive (meningitis 10%, bacteremia 20%, cutaneous abscess 15%). Autoimmunity included autoimmune hemolytic anemia (20%), thrombocytopenia (10%) and psoriasis (10%). Hypogammaglobulinemia was present in 20% and HPV warts in 25%. Myelokathexis was not observed.
quotes: Immune-mediated disease (95%) is widely present in MAGIS as both immunodeficiency (90%) and immune dysregulation (50%; systemic autoinflammation, 15%, autoimmunity, 35%, and splenomegaly, 35%).

Autoimmune manifestations included life-threatening autoimmune hemolytic anemia (20%), autoimmune thrombocytopenia (10%), psoriasis (10%), and Hashimoto’s thyroiditis, type I diabetes mellitus, alopecia, celiac disease, and autoimmune enteritis in individual patients to date.
Hypogammaglobulinemia is also present in both diseases, affecting 20% of known MAGIS patients compared with 58–89% in WHIM syndrome.

findings.statement: Lamborn et al. (2025) reported that lymphocyte immunophenotyping typically showed low or normal T cells that often improved with age, a low naive-to-memory T cell ratio, and low B cells with low serum IgM. Monocytes and neutrophils tended to be high or normal. Mitogen- and antigen-induced proliferation was normal or increased. One patient had an abnormal newborn SCID screen. Premature mortality was 10% in the original cohort.
quotes: In general, lymphocyte immunophenotyping in peripheral blood demonstrates low/normal T cells often with improvement with age, low naïve-to-memory T cell ratio, and low B cells with associated low serum IgM.
Newborn screen for severe combined immunodeficiency (SCID) was abnormal in one patient, who had an absolute T cell count of 0.577 × 103 cells/µl at 7 wk of age
While we observed a relatively low premature mortality (10% in our original cohort of 20 patients)

findings.statement: Lamborn et al. (2025) described intrafamilial variability in family XIII, in which a proband (P13) and his father (P14) both carried GNAI2 Arg179Cys. At 2 years P13 had IUGR, congenital heart valve abnormalities with hydrops fetalis, dysmorphism, hypospadias, severe congenital sensorineural hearing loss, neurodevelopmental delay, a small pons, a thin corpus callosum, and neonatal infections with pan-lymphocytopenia. His father had dysmorphism, osteoporosis, cryptorchidism, hearing loss, borderline intellectual disability, epilepsy, short stature, annular pancreas with bowel malrotation, recurrent infections and celiac disease.
quotes: In family XIII, both the affected proband (P13) and his father (P14) carry the Arg179Cys mutation

P14 also had growth delay with short stature, an annular pancreas with malrotation of the bowel and esophageal hiatal hernia, gastroesophageal reflux with aspiration pneumonias, recurrent infections (sinusitis, otitis media, tonsillitis, paronychia; lymphocyte numbers not measured), and celiac disease.

findings.statement: Lamborn et al. (2025) described family XVII, in which 2 brothers (P18, P19) carried GNAI2 Arg179His. P18 had dysmorphism, cryptorchidism, inguinal hernia, pelvic kidney, short stature, arthritis, sensorineural hearing loss, recurrent infections and dysgammaglobulinemia. His deceased brother had IUGR, short stature, neurodevelopmental delay, epilepsy, ataxia, autism, psychosis, mild splenomegaly, recurrent infections, dysgammaglobulinemia and T cell lymphopenia.
quotes: Another illustrative example is family XVII, in which two affected brothers (P18, P19) carried the Arg179His mutation

Overall, both patients shared dysmorphism with cryptorchidism, inguinal hernia, chronic diarrhea, growth delay, anxiety and depression, and recurrent infections with dysgammaglobulinemia, but features only present in one individual include the arthritis in P18 or the neurodevelopmental delay and T cell lymphopenia in P19.

findings.statement: Lamborn et al. (2025) noted that each of the 20 patients, who were of multiple ancestries, carried an extremely rare heterozygous missense GNAI2 variant. All variants were absent from population databases except Arg179His, which was found in 2 individuals in gnomAD v4.1.0 (MAF 0.000001281). Mutations recurred at Thr182 (Thr182Ala/Ile/Pro in 6 families) and Arg179 (Arg179His/Cys in 7 patients from 5 families). Most variants arose de novo.
quotes: Each patient carried an extremely rare or not previously reported heterozygous missense variant in GNAI2, with pathogenic predictions by several computational algorithms validated by extensive biochemical testing
with mutations recurring among unrelated patients often observed at residues Thr182 (Thr182Ala/Ile/Pro in six families) and Arg179 (Arg179His/Cys in seven patients from five families)
except for rs137853227 (Arg179His), which was found in two individuals in gnomAD v4.1.0, accessed March 2025 (minor allele frequency 0.000001281

findings.statement: Lamborn et al. (2025) observed full penetrance. Most variants arose de novo, but transmission of Arg179Cys from father to son and the presence of Arg179His in 2 brothers were consistent with autosomal dominant inheritance.
quotes: However, in our patient cohort one family had the Arg179Cys mutation in father and son, and another family had the Arg179His mutation in two brothers (described in the preceding section), consistent with an autosomal dominant inheritance pattern.

findings.statement: Lamborn et al. (2025) summarized that the mutant Gαi2 proteins bind GTP up to 20-fold faster and hydrolyze GTP up to 100-fold slower than wildtype, and that most are insensitive to RGS GAPs, making them constitutively active. The Arg179His and Arg179Cys mutants were less severely activating: they bound GTP more slowly and remained GAP-sensitive. The authors suggested this explained their transmission through generations.
quotes: Biochemical analysis demonstrated that mutant Gαi2 binds GTP up to 20-fold faster than wild-type (WT) and hydrolyzes GTP up to 100-fold slower than WT Gαi2.
The Arg179His and Arg179Cys Gαi2 proteins bind GTP more slowly than WT Gαi2 and remain sensitive to the GTP hydrolysis–promoting effects of GAPs

findings.statement: Lamborn et al. (2025) summarized that MAGIS T cells and neutrophils showed impaired chemotaxis and chemokine-induced calcium flux because the mutant Gαi2 stays decoupled from GPCRs, a mechanism functionally resembling CXCR4 signaling deficiency. Separately, mutant Gαi2 sequestered RASA2 and enhanced TCR-induced RAS, ERK/MAPK and PI3K/AKT/S6 signaling, causing T cell hyperresponsiveness that may underlie autoimmunity. Knocking out adenylyl cyclases AC3 and AC7 in T cells did not reproduce these defects, suggesting they were independent of cAMP.
quotes: MAGIS mutant proteins remain predominantly decoupled from GPCRs at steady state, consistent with their biochemically activated state.
we identified RASA2, a GAP for RAS, as an effector target of Gαi2, and found that active Gαi2 inhibits RASA2-mediated negative regulation of S6-regulatory signaling and T cell activation.
These data suggest the impaired chemotaxis and T cell hyperresponsiveness of MAGIS syndrome are independent of cAMP and related to the mechanisms described above.

findings.statement: Lamborn et al. (2025) reported one MAGIS patient who received HSCT from a fully matched unrelated donor and achieved full donor chimerism. The transplant eradicated granulomatous skin disease caused by vaccine-strain rubella and resolved recurrent infections. Autoimmune hemolytic anemia stayed in remission for more than 3 years, while nonimmune features were unaffected. In vitro, selective CRISPR deletion of the mutant allele or combined RAS/MAPK and PI3K/AKT inhibition corrected T cell hyperresponsiveness.
quotes: Results were encouraging for one MAGIS patient who received fully matched unrelated donor stem cells and achieved full donor chimerism

HSCT successfully eradicated the patient’s granulomatous skin disease caused by vaccine-strain rubella virus, as well as his recurrent upper respiratory tract infections, otitis media, and bronchitis.

Furthermore, inhibitors of the RAS/ERK/MAPK and PI3K/AKT pathways were each able to partially correct the T cell hyperresponsiveness in vitro, although both inhibitors were required for complete correction

relevance_reason: The abstract names FEM1B as a good candidate gene for syndromic intellectual disability, based on recurrent de novo missense variants. It gives no patient or variant details.

findings.statement: Lecoquierre et al. (2019) searched their database of more than 1,200 solo exomes and the public denovo-db collection of de novo variants from patients with developmental disorders for the same missense variant in unrelated individuals with similar phenotypes. They found 30 variants with strong evidence of pathogenicity and identified FEM1B as a good candidate gene for syndromic intellectual disability.
quotes: We looked for variations independently present in both our database of >1200 solo exomes and in denovo-db, a large, publicly available collection of de novo variants identified in patients with DD.
We identified FEM1B and GNAI2 as good candidate genes for syndromic intellectual disability and confirmed the implication of ACTL6B in a neurodevelopmental disorder.

relevance_reason: Reports a de novo heterozygous GNAI2 missense variant in a patient with periventricular nodular heterotopia and intellectual disability, plus functional knockdown studies of Galphai2 in the mouse cortex.

findings.statement: In an individual with periventricular nodular heterotopia and intellectual disability, Hamada et al. (2017) used whole-exome sequencing to identify a de novo heterozygous missense mutation (c.680C>T; p.Ala227Val) in the GNAI2 gene, which encodes Galphai2.
quotes: using whole-exome sequencing analysis, we identified a de novo heterozygous missense mutation (c.680C>T; p.Ala227Val) in the GNAI2 gene encoding Gαi2 in an individual with periventricular nodular heterotopia and intellectual disability

findings.statement: Hamada et al. (2017) found that acute knockdown of Galphai2 by in utero electroporation in mice caused delayed radial migration of excitatory neurons during corticogenesis, possibly because of impaired morphology; an RNAi-resistant Galphai2 rescued the migration defect. Silencing Galphai2 did not affect axon elongation, dendritic arbor formation, or neurogenesis at the ventricular zone in vivo.
quotes: Acute knockdown of the α-subunit (Gαi2) with in utero electroporation caused delayed radial migration of excitatory neurons during corticogenesis, perhaps because of impaired morphology.
The migration phenotype was rescued by an RNAi-resistant version of Gαi2.
silencing of Gαi2 did not affect axon elongation, dendritic arbor formation or neurogenesis at ventricular zone in vivo

findings.statement: Hamada et al. (2017) reported that mice with acute Galphai2 knockdown had defects in social interaction, novelty recognition, and active avoidance learning, along with increased anxiety. The authors suggested that impaired Galphai2 function might cause defects in neuronal function that lead to neurodevelopmental disorders.
quotes: When behavior analyses were conducted with acute Gαi2-knockdown mice, they showed defects in social interaction, novelty recognition and active avoidance learning as well as increased anxiety.
impairment of its function might cause defects in neuronal functions which lead to neurodevelopmental disorders
